where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.hypoglycaemia_dm, suggest_against[0] (vs.glucose >= REF-EX-HYPO-L1)
finding: Any recorded glucose of 3.9 mmol/L or more is offered as evidence AGAINST hypoglycaemia in a person with diabetes. The atom has no timing or treatment qualifier, and the briefing does not say which reading the vital atom takes when there are several (presumably the latest). The profile's own note says the atom 'holds only for a glucose taken while symptomatic and BEFORE treatment' and that 'the evidence text must say so', but nothing in the atom, the engine-change list or the text field delivers that.
why: dx.hypoglycaemia_dm is must-not-miss and time-critical. The usual patient has already had sugar at home, at triage or in resus before the clerking glucose is taken, so the first recorded value is often normal. If the atom reads the latest value, then after treatment the 'for' mark (hypoglycaemia_level) disappears and an 'against' mark appears in the same column. A junior can then mark the diagnosis unlikely with a three-word reason and discharge a patient on glibenclamide or long-acting insulin, in whom the low recurs for many hours. This is the opposite of what the STOP report gap was meant to close.
fix: Remove the atom from this amendment. Re-add it only with an engine change that lets the glucose vital carry 'taken before any sugar, glucose or glucagon was given' and 'taken while symptomatic', and make the atom true only when both are recorded yes (unknown otherwise). Put the caveat in the evidence text itself, not in the profile note. Apply the same timing rule to the dx.dka 'against' atom (blood ketones below REF-DX-KETONE-NORMAL), which also reads the latest value and can be normal after treatment at a referring unit.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, classifiers.add.dr_review; flag FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT; clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DR-REFER
finding: The 'Retinopathy: next step' classifier reads only dr_grade, macula=centre_involving and view=inadequate, first match wins. It therefore returns 'review_1_to_2_years' for mild retinopathy with (a) macula = non_centre (oedema or exudate, centre spared), (b) macula = cannot_assess, (c) visual acuity worse than 6/12 or visual symptoms, and (d) an undilated direct view. It returns nothing at all when the clinician ticks the existing option seen = not_visualised instead of the new view = inadequate. CARE-DR-REFER repeats the same three grade windows and also omits non-centre oedema and the acuity rule, although it cites REF-DM-EYE-REFER-VA.
why: The pack's own dossier says otherwise: REF-DM-EYE-RECALL-DME-NCI (ICO: non-centre-involving oedema re-examined in 3 months, referral recommended where laser exists), REF-DM-EYE-REFER-VA (refer if acuity is worse than 6/12 or there are visual symptoms, whatever the grade), REF-DM-EYE-REFER-NOVIEW (refer if acuity or an adequate view cannot be obtained), REF-DM-EYE-CONTROLLED-ONLY (the schedule applies only where diabetes is controlled) and REF-DM-EYE-METHOD (dilated ophthalmoscopy or photography by a trained person). The dx.diabetic_retinopathy note itself says 'a normal undilated direct ophthalmoscopy misses most retinopathy' and 'vision worse than 6/12 or any visual symptom is referred whatever the grade'. A screen that tells a clerking doctor 'review in 1 to 2 years' for a patient with macular oedema or reduced acuity delays sight-saving treatment. REF-EX-DR-RECALL already holds dme_non_centre = 3 months but no rule reads it.
fix: Rewrite the classifier in this order: (1) refer within 1 month: pdr or macula centre_involving; (2) refer within 3 months: severe_npdr; (3) refer: macula cannot_assess, view inadequate, seen includes not_visualised, or visual acuity worse than 6/12 in either eye, or sym.blurred_vision yes; (4) re-examine in 3 months: macula non_centre; (5) moderate; (6) mild only when method is dilated or photograph AND view adequate AND acuity recorded 6/12 or better in both eyes; otherwise result 'incomplete' (as iwgdf_risk does). Take every interval from REF-EX-DR-RECALL rather than from the result id. Show the 'applies only where diabetes is controlled' caveat in the result reason. Add non-centre oedema and the acuity rule to CARE-DR-REFER. Make FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT fire on rule 3 as well. Decide with the CSO whether Uganda's 2016 guideline (refer every person with diabetes to a retina centre) or ICO is the default and model both, rather than leaving the Uganda rule in a note.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json, every item whose problems include dx.dm_type1, dx.dm_type_unknown or dx.dm_type2 (CARE-DM-TARGET, CARE-DM-BP, CARE-DM-EYE, CARE-DM-KIDNEY, CARE-DM-LIPIDS, CARE-DM-CVD-RISK, CARE-DM-HYPO-REVIEW, CARE-DM-REVIEW, CARE-DM-MEDS-REVIEW, CARE-DM-STATIN)
finding: No item in the suggested-care list has an age gate, and no clerking file contains one. A child or a 14-year-old with dx.dm_type1 on the board is shown adult management content: 'treat towards below 130/80', 'agree an individual target', adult eye and kidney screening intervals, the adult cardiovascular risk chart and the adult review cadence.
why: Pack rule 3 and briefing Part 4.1: under 16 is recognition, classification support and referral only, with no management content. Most diabetes in children is type 1, and the dx.dka note itself anticipates children. Adult blood-pressure and glycaemic targets and adult screening start times are wrong for children. If the adult desk never clerks anyone under 16 this must be stated and enforced by the engine, not assumed.
fix: Add a 'when' with a signed age reference (16 years) to every management, target, screening-interval and recall item, and add one under-16 item for the three diabetes problems: 'Under 16: refer to the paediatric or diabetes team today' (kind refer). Add a vignette of a 12-year-old with dx.dm_type1 showing that only recognition, ketone testing, education and referral items appear. State in the pack whether the adult v2 desk can be opened for a patient under 16.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.hhs, suggest_against[0] (classifier ketone_band = dka_range)
finding: Ketones in the 'dka_range' band are offered as evidence AGAINST the hyperosmolar state, while the same profile's note says ketones in that range 'point to a mixed picture, which is common and more dangerous: keep both on the board'. The band also includes a urine strip of 2+ with no blood value.
why: dx.hhs is must-not-miss and time-critical. Mixed ketoacidosis and hyperosmolar state is common; a urine strip of 2+ is frequent in a vomiting, starved hyperosmolar patient. The matrix would nudge a junior to mark the hyperosmolar state unlikely exactly when the note says not to. The atom and the note contradict each other.
fix: Delete the 'against' atom. If the CSO wants the 2024 consensus exclusion shown, show ketone_band as neutral context on the HHS card with the text 'ketones raised: consider a mixed picture', never as an 'against' mark.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.dm_type1, suggest_against[0] (res:obs.c_peptide >= REF-DX-CPEP-HIGH); REF-DX-CPEP-LOW; REF-DX-CPEP-HIGH
finding: A random C-peptide at or above 600 pmol/L is evidence AGAINST type 1 with only min_trust as a condition. The REF text requires a concurrent glucose and a sample within 5 hours of eating, and the source applies the bands to people on insulin some years after diagnosis; none of that is in the atom, and there is no maximum age for the result. REF-DX-CPEP-LOW says a low value 'indicates type 1' without saying that a low value during a hyperglycaemic crisis or with a low concurrent glucose is not interpretable (the dossier rates this entry confidence 'low').
why: dx.dm_type1 is set must-not-miss in this amendment because missing it leads to ketoacidosis. C-peptide is preserved early in type 1 and is raised by kidney impairment. An 'against' mark from an early or unpaired sample can lead to insulin being withdrawn.
fix: Remove the 'against' atom, or make it conditional on atoms the engine can check (on insulin, year_diagnosed at least the source's interval ago, paired glucose recorded). Until then show C-peptide as a result on the card with the source's conditions in the evidence text. Fix the REF-DX-CPEP-LOW meaning to carry the source's conditions and its 'low' confidence.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.hhs suggest_for (res:derived.osmolality_effective > REF-DX-OSM-HHS); REF-DX-OSM-HHS; wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json derived.osmolality_effective
finding: The atom compares EFFECTIVE osmolality (2 x sodium + glucose, the concept proposed in the CFC addendum) with REF-DX-OSM-HHS, whose value 320 mOsm/kg is the TOTAL osmolality threshold (2 x sodium + glucose + urea, mirror of REF-DM-ACU-HHS-OSM-TOTAL). The atom text also names a third thing, 'derived.osmolality'.
why: The dossier holds both thresholds: effective above 300 (REF-DM-ACU-HHS-OSM-EFF) or total above 320. An effective osmolality of 305 to 320 meets the criterion and would not be marked. Formula and threshold do not match.
fix: Either compare derived.osmolality_effective with a new REF-DX-OSM-HHS-EFF (mirror of REF-DM-ACU-HHS-OSM-EFF), or propose derived.osmolality_total and keep 320. State the formula in the REF meaning and make the atom text name the same concept as the atom.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profiles dx.dm_type_unknown and dx.dm_type2, suggest_against (res:obs.glucose(ogtt_2h) < REF-DX-GLU-2H-IGT); note on dx.dm_type_unknown
finding: A 2-hour value below 7.8 mmol/L alone is offered as evidence against diabetes. It is not conditional on the fasting value of the same test, on HbA1c, or on the patient not taking glucose-lowering treatment. The note says 'only a normal 2-hour OGTT counts against'.
why: A person with a fasting value of 7.0 or more and a 2-hour value below 7.8 still has a diabetes-range result (isolated fasting hyperglycaemia). A normal 2-hour value in someone on metformin or a sulfonylurea refutes nothing. The matrix would show 'against' beside a diabetes-range fasting result from the same test.
fix: Make the 'against' atom an 'all': 2-hour below REF-DX-GLU-2H-IGT AND fasting value of the same test below REF-DX-GLU-FASTING-IFG AND medicine_group glucose_lowering recorded not taken. Correct the note to 'a normal OGTT (fasting and 2-hour) off treatment'.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.dm_type2 suggest_for (cls:waist_risk, cls:bmi_who, pmh:diabetes, glucose and HbA1c atoms) compared with dx.dm_type1 suggest_for
finding: Type 2 lists waist band, BMI band, family history, past diabetes of any type, capillary glucose, laboratory glucose and HbA1c as evidence. Type 1 lists none of the glucose, HbA1c or past-diabetes atoms. So for any person with known diabetes and a raised glucose the type 2 column fills with several suggested marks and the type 1 column stays empty, and build adds two more to type 2.
why: Pack rule 6 and briefing Part 4.2: type is never inferred from build; return unclassified rather than infer from phenotype. Glucose and HbA1c establish diabetes, not its type. The dx.dm_type_unknown note says 'build alone does not decide it in Uganda' and the type 2 note says a third of Ugandan adults with non-autoimmune diabetes are lean. An evidence count that is built to be lopsided will steer juniors to type 2 in a young, overweight, ketosis-prone or type 1 patient.
fix: Keep the diabetes-establishing atoms (glucose, HbA1c, past diabetes) on dx.dm_type_unknown only, or put the identical set on both type profiles. Remove waist and BMI bands from type 2 evidence, or show them as context that is never counted. Leave on each type profile only discriminating evidence: reported type, insulin from diagnosis, ketones, C-peptide and antibodies under their conditions.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profiles dx.dm_type_unknown, dx.dm_type2, dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy and rule DDX-RESULT-HBA1C (res:obs.hba1c >= REF-DX-HBA1C-DM); clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json EC-1
finding: The dx.dm_type_unknown note promises that 'the engine shows the HbA1c with its date and marks it not usable for diagnosis with the reason' in pregnancy, haemoglobin variants, haemolysis, recent malaria or transfusion, iron or B12 deficiency and low eGFR. EC-1 specifies no such behaviour. The atom has only min_trust 3, which admits a point-of-care HbA1c, has no maximum age (REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-HBA1C is defined and used by nothing) and reads no certification or method context.
why: Iron deficiency, sickle trait, malaria and pregnancy are common in Uganda and move HbA1c in both directions. As written, an HbA1c of 6.5% or more in an iron-deficient or pregnant patient is a plain suggested 'for' mark, and the safeguard exists only as a sentence in a note. The CFC already carries 'certification' and 'method' for HbA1c.
fix: Add the validity behaviour to EC-1 as a specified, tested rule: a list of signed caveat atoms per concept that turns the result to 'not usable for diagnosis' with the reason, or drop the sentence from the note. Require certification or laboratory method for the diagnostic atom. State how a restricted caveat (for example antiretroviral treatment) is shown without breaking the rule that no restricted fact is evidence on a standard diagnosis.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profiles dx.gestational_diabetes and dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy; rules DDX-RESULT-GLUCOSE-FASTING, DDX-RESULT-GLUCOSE-IFG; clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DKD-RASI, CARE-DM-STATIN, CARE-GDM-POSTPARTUM; clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json
finding: There is no pregnancy atom. The two pregnancy profiles say 'offered only in a pregnant patient' but nothing gates them and no differential rule suggests them. Their result atoms have no maximum age, so a value from before the pregnancy or from an earlier pregnancy counts. A pregnant woman with a fasting value of 5.1 to 6.0 gets no suggestion; at 6.1 to 6.9 she is offered 'intermediate hyperglycaemia'; at 7.0 or more she is offered dx.dm_type_unknown rather than the must-not-miss dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy. dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy lacks past diabetes and the symptomatic random value as evidence. The care items that prompt an ACE inhibitor, ARB or statin review cannot exclude pregnancy. The gap is noted only as '_reconcile: how pregnancy gates a profile' and is not in the engine-change list.
why: Applying non-pregnant thresholds and labels to a pregnant woman is a clinical error in both directions. The record already holds pregnancy facts (pregnancy_episodes), so the engine can know.
fix: Add EC-5: a 'pregnancy {state}' atom reading the current pregnancy episode, unknown when no episode is recorded. Gate both pregnancy profiles and a new DDX rule on it; bound the result atoms to the current episode; make the non-pregnant DDX result rules and dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia require 'not pregnant' recorded, or show a 'pregnancy not recorded' caveat for women of reproductive age. Add 'not in pregnancy' to the CARE-DKD-RASI and CARE-DM-STATIN labels. Until EC-5 exists withhold both pregnancy profiles.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, every profile with _op 'amend' (dx.dm_type_unknown, dx.dm_type2, dx.dm_type1, dx.dka, dx.hhs, dx.hypoglycaemia_dm, dx.ckd) and ddx_rules.amend
finding: 'amend' is not defined as replace or merge. Six profiles are written as complete objects; dx.ckd is written as a complete object holding only two evidence atoms, one ask, one test and one related diagnosis, with a note saying 'existing content is unchanged'. If the loader replaces, the signed dx.ckd profile loses all its present content; if it merges, the six diabetes profiles keep whatever atoms they hold today, which the author could not see (the briefing shows only dx.hypertension verbatim). The dx.ckd note adds 'a second named scale' but severity holds one scale id, and kdigo_albuminuria is attached to no profile. dx.dm_type1 is changed to must_not_miss true without being listed as a decision, and the new rules that suggest it (DDX-KETONES, DDX-RESULT-HBA1C, DDX-RESULT-GLUCOSE-FASTING) do not list it in must_not_miss_first.
why: The live profiles are CSO-signed and every one of their 1,910 atoms is tested. An amendment that silently drops or keeps atoms cannot be reviewed for clinical sense, and a must-not-miss change alters the signing block for every note that carries the diagnosis.
fix: Regenerate this file against the live catalogue JSON as an explicit diff per profile: atoms added, atoms removed with the reason, fields changed from and to. Express dx.ckd as 'suggest_for.add' and 'tests_to_decide.add' in the same style as ddx_rules.amend. List the must-not-miss change to dx.dm_type1 and the new must-not-miss dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy as numbered CSO decisions, and update must_not_miss_first in every rule that suggests them. Either propose the schema change for two named scales or drop the sentence.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-CONFIRM; clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json profile dx.dm_type2 and dx.dm_type1 notes
finding: The 'repeat on another day' item is attached only to dx.dm_type_unknown and dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed. A clinician who picks 'Type 2 diabetes' directly on one raised value in a person without symptoms gets no confirm item, and the dx.dm_type2 note does not carry the confirmation rule. The item opens test.glucose_fasting whatever the first test was, although its label says 'same test preferred', and it shows on dx.dm_type_unknown even when the diagnosis is already secure (symptoms with a value of 11.1 or more, or long-known diabetes).
why: Pack rule 5: a single abnormal value must not diagnose a person without symptoms. The safeguard depends on which of three labels the clinician happens to choose.
fix: Attach the item to all three diabetes problems with a 'when' that hides it once past diabetes is recorded yes; state the confirmation rule in the type 2 and type 1 notes; let the item open the same test as the first abnormal result.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, classifiers.add.ketone_band (result dka_range) and flag FLAG-EX-KETONES-DKA; rule DDX-KETONES in 09-diagnosis.amendment.json
finding: A urine ketone strip of 2+ or 3+ alone puts anyone in the band named 'dka_range' and raises an urgent flag: 'Ketones in the ketoacidosis range: check a venous gas or bicarbonate and get senior review now'. There is no glucose or diabetes condition. The pack's own acute rule acu_ketones (catalog/60-acute-route.json) requires glucose of 11.1 or more, or known diabetes, alongside the ketones. The urine branches name no reference entry, so the 2+ threshold cannot be withheld and is not signed (REF-DM-ACU-DKA-UKET exists in the dossier but has no REF-EX mirror). The exam composer prints classifier bands beside vitals (the briefing's example is 'BMI 21.1 (normal weight)'), so a fasting or vomiting non-diabetic could have a 'ketoacidosis range' band written into the note.
why: Starvation, vomiting, hyperemesis, fasting and gastroenteritis commonly give 2+ urine ketones with a normal glucose. Urgent (red) is reserved for findings worth interrupting a clinician; this one would fire on many non-diabetic patients and teach staff to ignore it. A band name that is a diagnosis breaks 'findings, not interpretations'.
fix: Rename the bands to findings (for example 'high', 'moderately raised', 'raised'). Keep urgent only for: blood ketones at or above REF-EX-KETONE-DKA, or urine 2+ or more, together with any of glucose at or above REF-EX-GLU-HIGH, past diabetes yes, medicine_group glucose_lowering, or Kussmaul breathing; otherwise caution with the text 'raised ketones: check glucose; consider starvation, vomiting, pregnancy and alcohol'. Add REF-EX-KETONE-URINE-DKA for the strip grade. At sites without a gas or bicarbonate the reason should end 'or refer', not assume a venous gas.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, flag FLAG-EX-INSULIN-STOPPED
finding: Urgent flag 'Insulin stopped: risk of ketoacidosis. Check glucose and ketones now' on any medicine entry for insulin with adherence 'stopped'. It has no condition on type, on who stopped it, on when, on symptoms or on glucose. It relies on a 'medicine + adherence_any' atom the shared evaluator is not shown to have (acknowledged in its note, not in the engine-change list). It names only REF-DM ids, and it duplicates the history rule FLAG-MED-ADHERENCE in a second engine.
why: A person with type 2 diabetes whose insulin was stopped by a doctor after a step-down, or a woman whose insulin stopped after delivery, would carry a red badge at every visit. The flag matters for type 1 or insulin from diagnosis, or with a raised glucose, vomiting or ketones.
fix: Make it urgent only when insulin is 'stopped' AND any of: past_detail type = type_1, insulin_from_start = yes, glucose at or above REF-EX-GLU-HIGH, sym.vomiting yes, or ketone band raised; otherwise leave the existing caution from FLAG-MED-ADHERENCE. Add the atom to 00-engine-changes.json. Give the badge the same text as FLAG-MED-ADHERENCE so the two merge.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, suggestion SUG-PMH-DIABETES, note ('Remove that branch [of SUG-POLYURIA] when this lands')
finding: The note asks for the past-diabetes branch of the signed rule SUG-POLYURIA to be removed. SUG-POLYURIA offers hydration, breathing pattern and odour; SUG-PMH-DIABETES does not. After the change a known diabetic who is unwell without polyuria (vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsy) gets no chip for hydration, Kussmaul breathing or ketotic breath unless the glucose is 18 or more (SUG-GLU-KETONES).
why: Those three examinations are how ketoacidosis is recognised at the bedside, and ketoacidosis occurs below 18 mmol/L. The change is also an edit to a signed rule hidden in a note rather than listed as an amendment. The 'why' text says 'eyes at every review', which contradicts the 24-month interval in REF-EX-DR-RECALL and CARE-DM-EYE.
fix: Keep the SUG-POLYURIA branch, or add a rule: past diabetes yes AND any of sym.vomiting, sym.abdominal_pain, sym.confusion, sym.breathlessness yes, or glucose at or above REF-EX-GLU-HIGH, offering vs.ketones, ex.general.hydration, ex.respiratory.breathing_pattern and ex.general.odour. List any change to SUG-POLYURIA under an explicit 'suggestion_rules.amend'. Change the 'why' to 'eyes when due'.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, medicine_groups.add (sglt2_inhibitor, insulin, sulfonylurea, systemic_steroid) and flags FLAG-EX-SGLT2-UNWELL, DDX-SGLT2-UNWELL, DDX-STEROID-GLUCOSE; clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json symptoms.also_ask.add (sglt2_tablet)
finding: The groups match generic name stems only. A medicine typed by brand, or a patient who knows only 'a tablet that makes sugar pass in the urine', is not in the group, so the urgent SGLT2 flag, its suggestion and its differential rule stay silent. The new also-ask item 'sglt2_tablet' on sym.polyuria is read by no rule. 'systemic_steroid' matches hydrocortisone cream, dexamethasone or prednisolone eye drops by stem, so the steroid rules fire on topical treatment. The flag covers only vomiting and abdominal pain, where the pack's acute rule acu_edka also lists deep rapid breathing and acute illness. The record already has drug class tags (sglt2_inhibitor, sulfonylurea, insulin, systemic_glucocorticoid) with different ids.
why: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis has a normal glucose, so the medicine is the only cue. A safety flag that depends on spelling is silent when it matters, and a steroid rule that cannot tell route cries wolf.
fix: Drive the groups from the medication statement's class tags where a drug code exists and fall back to stems only for free text; add the common brand stems as a signed list; let 'medicine_group' also be satisfied by the also-ask answer (or move that question into the medicines step as 'takes an SGLT2 inhibitor: yes, no, not sure'). Restrict 'systemic_steroid' to oral or injected routes. Add breathlessness, drowsiness and reduced eating or drinking to FLAG-EX-SGLT2-UNWELL so it matches acu_edka.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json REF-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST, FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST, SUG-GLU-KETONES; clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json DDX-GLUCOSE-VERY-HIGH (REF-DX-GLU-HHS), dx.hhs suggest_for
finding: All of these compare a numeric vs.glucose with 18 or 33.3 mmol/L. A bedside meter does not give a number at the top of its range; it shows 'HI'. vs.glucose is a number field (plausible 0.5 to 50) with no way to record 'meter reads HI', and the amendment proposes none.
why: The hyperosmolar threshold sits at or above the ceiling of most meters, and district sites have only a meter. The sickest patients are the ones for whom every one of these rules has nothing to read, unless the clinician invents a number.
fix: Add a 'reads HI' (and 'reads LO') qualifier to vs.glucose that stores no invented number and that the vital atom treats as at or above every upper threshold (and LO as below every lower one). Add it to the engine-change list and to the tests.

where: clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json (EC-1 to EC-4) against all amendment files
finding: The amendments use engine features that the briefing does not show and that the engine-change list does not declare. History: applies_to 'past_history'; 'shown_when' on a history property; 'includes_any' in the history language; a per-condition 'composer' template. Exam: a new vitals panel vs.ketones with a coded urine field (saved by vitals.ts saveLines); panel atoms with 'field'; 'panel ... recorded' (noted in the rule only); 'medicine' with 'adherence_any' (noted in the rule only); two new classifiers, although the briefing says all classifiers live in lib/clerking/exam/classifiers.ts; 'option_sets' and 'options_ref' in the exam catalogue; token-map entries with 'value_from_option'; a composer rule for 'no retinopathy seen (undilated)'; 'why' and 'refs_dm' keys on suggestion rules; 'system', 'concept' and 'source' keys on items. Diagnosis: 'setting' with a list; 'ask' kinds 'panel' and 'past_detail'; 'panel field lt_ref'; a second named scale on one profile; amend operations. Plan: 'patient {age_gte_ref}' (the evaluator has patient.age_gte and the history language has age_gte_ref, not this); 'opens.disposition' and 'opens.followUp' with free-text values and no rule on overwriting what the clinician already set; keys 'refs_dm', 'ncd_step' and 'where_unavailable' that EC-4's own item shape does not list (it lists 'refs'). Formulary: a 'ketone row' on the glucose chart. EC-1 says it reads 'the latest fact for the concept' and then applies 'context', which would let a later random glucose hide an earlier fasting one; and its 'context' values do not exist in the fact model, which uses fastingState, challenge {ogtt_75g | meal, minutes} and specimen.
why: Briefing Part 2 section 0: content needs no code change only if it uses existing response types and rule atoms; Part 4.2: if the grammar cannot express something, say so and propose the change. Undeclared atoms either fail the catalogue schema or evaluate as never true, so the rule is silently dead; unknown keys may simply be stripped (the briefing notes this for the note schema).
fix: Extend 00-engine-changes.json with one entry per item above (or remove the use), each with its evaluator, schema and test. In EC-1 define the atom over the real context keys: fasting = fastingState fasting; ogtt_2h = challenge ogtt_75g at 120 minutes; add 'specimen'; read the latest fact that MATCHES the qualifiers; say what a comparator value ('<', '>') does. Mark every rule and profile atom that depends on an engine change with 'needs', as the DDX result rules already do (the profile atoms and the plan items do not).

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json result and vital atoms with 'context'; wiring/test-menu.additions.json test.glucose_capillary and test.ogtt_75g; wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json qualifiersNeeded
finding: Three vocabularies name the 2-hour post-load glucose: 'two_hours_after_food' (vs.glucose), 'two_hours_after_glucose' (test.glucose_capillary) and 'ogtt_2h' (test.ogtt_75g and every result atom). A capillary 2-hour value entered through the meter test never matches the 'ogtt_2h' atoms. No atom carries the specimen, so the venous threshold REF-DX-GLU-2H-DM (11.1) is applied to any obs.glucose at 2 hours, while the pack's confirm lane uses 12.2 mmol/L for capillary samples (catalog/20-confirm.json) and the addendum itself records 'the 2-hour capillary threshold differs (12.2 against 11.1)'. No context-qualified atom reads 'two_hours_after_food', so a capillary value of 15 two hours after a meal is not evidence on any diabetes profile.
why: The clerking desk and the NCD engine would give different answers for the same capillary result between 11.1 and 12.1, and a meter-only district site cannot produce OGTT evidence at all.
fix: Use one context vocabulary taken from the fact model. Add 'specimen' to the result atom and a REF-DX-GLU-2H-DM-CAPILLARY entry mirroring the confirm lane. Decide and state whether a 2-hour post-meal capillary value counts as a random value for the symptomatic rule, and add that atom.

where: clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json, 07-exam.amendment.json, 09-diagnosis.amendment.json, 10-plan-care.v1.json: keys 'refs_dm', 'ref_dm', 'mirrors'; plan-care labels
finding: Thirty-two REF-EX and REF-DX entries are copies of REF-DM dossier entries, linked only by a 'mirrors' key, so each number would be signed twice in two catalogues and can drift. Rules also carry 'refs_dm' naming REF-DM ids that no clerking sign-off file knows: the briefing says engines find references by pattern over the rule JSON and a rule fires only when every reference it names is signed. Depending on the pattern, those rules are either never live or not gated at all. Several flags name only REF-DM ids (FLAG-EX-INSULIN-STOPPED, FLAG-EX-SGLT2-UNWELL, both history flags). The Plan care list has no reference entries at all: about a dozen thresholds live in label text ('below 130/80', '18', 'at 40 or over', 'every 2 years', 'within 1 month ... 3 months ... 6 to 12 months', '2 of 3 within 3 to 6 months', '2 to 4 weeks', '6 to 12 weeks', '3 months (6 months ...; 1 month ...)', '12 months'). Rule 'why' and flag 'reason' strings repeat thresholds as text ('HbA1c 6.5% or more', 'Glucose 18 mmol/L or more'). Two mirrors cite a different source from the dossier entry they copy (REF-DX-KETONE-NORMAL: ADA-EASD-CRISES-2024 against TREND-UK; REF-DX-CPEP-HIGH: ADA-EASD-T1-2021 against ADA 2026). Six entries are defined and used by no rule: REF-DX-EGFR-REFER, REF-DX-K-SEVERE, REF-DX-KETONE-DKA, REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-HBA1C, REF-DX-UACR-A3, REF-EX-IPSWICH. REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-GLUCOSE has no value, so every rule and atom that names it (the laboratory fasting and OGTT evidence) is dead until the CSO supplies one; meanwhile the same glucose result is evidence at any age on the profiles that omit max_age_ref (dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia, both pregnancy profiles) and every HbA1c atom has no age limit.
why: Ground rule: every threshold is a reference entry, and the withheld list is the kill switch. A number in a label cannot be withheld and does not change when the CSO changes the reference. Briefing 3.6: attribution errors are the real risk.
fix: Choose one home for each number. Either the clerking catalogues hold REF-EX/REF-DX entries generated from the dossier by a build step that fails on drift (source and value copied, never retyped), or the clerking engines learn to resolve REF-DM ids against the signed dossier. Give the Plan care list 'refs' to signed entries and build label numbers from them with placeholders, as badges already do. Remove or use the six orphan entries. List the rules that are dead until REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-GLUCOSE is set.

where: Ids across clerking-v2/*.json and wiring/*.json that the briefing does not show and that are not marked for reconciliation
finding: Not shown to exist and not marked: sym.vomiting and sym.abdominal_pain (used by an urgent flag, a suggestion, a differential rule and dx.dka; the briefing shows them only as red-flag ids on sym.polyuria); dx.sepsis, dx.malaria_severe, dx.cataract (in 'related'); the setting values 'emergency' and 'inpatient'; finding 'ex.general.hydration is positive' (the item's response type is not shown; a classifier dehydration_gtfcc exists); REF-EX-HYPO-L1 used inside the diagnosis catalogue (cross-catalogue reference and sign-off); formulary classes gabapentinoid, snri, tricyclic_antidepressant (the link says only 'add the classes if absent'). The two symptom ids very probably exist, but an urgent rule should not rest on a guess. The eight new diagnoses (dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia, dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed, dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia, dx.gestational_diabetes, dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy, dx.diabetic_retinopathy, dx.diabetic_kidney_disease, dx.diabetic_neuropathy) point at REF-DX-TERMS but the pack contains no term entries for them: no display label, synonyms or code, and no term addendum or migration. Marked for reconciliation and still open: sym.dizziness, sym.numbness, ex.nervous.reflexes, breathing_pattern attribute and option ids, waist_risk and bmi_who band ids, categories obstetric, eye and neurological.
why: The catalogue check resolves every sym, ex, classifier, dx and test id across catalogues and fails CI on the first miss. A profile with no term has no name to render.
fix: Run the amendment against the live catalogues and replace every guessed id. Add a REF-DX-TERMS addendum with the eight terms and their seed migration to the pack. Where the symptom is only a red flag today, either add the symptom or write the atom as the red-flag form ('symptom ... red_flag').

where: wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json conceptsToPropose and qualifiersNeeded; clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json vs.ketones urine options, fundoscopy macula options, token_map.add
finding: The addendum proposes as new five concepts the briefing's concept list (Part 1, section 2.5) shows as already present (obs.c_peptide, obs.islet_autoantibody, obs.chol_total, exam.ankle_reflex, soc.physical_activity) and says of total cholesterol that it 'does not' exist. It proposes exam.macular_oedema beside the existing exam.maculopathy. It asks for 'specimen' and a new 'context' qualifier on obs.glucose although specimen, fastingState and challenge already exist. Option ids do not line up: urine ketones are 'negative, trace, 1+, 2+, 3+' as bare strings on the panel, 'neg, trace, 1plus, 2plus, 3plus' in catalog/01-features.json and '2plus' in the dossier; macula is 'no_oedema, non_centre, centre_involving, cannot_assess' on the exam item and 'none, non_centre, centre_involving' on the concept; view is 'adequate, inadequate' on the item and adds 'not_attempted' on the concept. The token map gives exam.retinal_view in the item's 'commit' block but not in token_map.add. EC-2 says nothing from per-condition detail is charted, while the addendum proposes hx.dm_type_reported, hx.dm_year_diagnosed and event.hypoglycaemia for exactly those answers.
why: Briefing Part 4.2: reuse existing concepts. The seed is insert-or-ignore, so a re-proposed concept with a different value type or unit is silently dropped. With 'value_from_option' a mismatched option id writes a code the concept does not accept, and signing counts it as 'unmapped: kept in the note, not charted'.
fix: Diff the addendum against lib/facts/catalogue.generated.ts and keep only concepts that are new. Reuse exam.maculopathy or justify the second concept. Use one id set for each option list across the exam item, the NCD feature and the concept. Give panel options the {id, label} shape. Resolve the EC-2 and addendum contradiction.

where: wiring/test-menu.additions.json (all 11 entries)
finding: Entries use a single 'result_concept' where the test catalogue has components[] (concept ids), fasting_required and capability_id; none of those is given. test.venous_gas returns only obs.ph_venous, so the bicarbonate that dx.dka reads has no ordered source; test.ogtt_75g has no fasting flag and one concept for three time points; test.xray_abdomen has no result concept (null); test.retinal_photograph returns only a grade, with no eye, macula, acuity or gradability, and combines a photograph with a dilated examination in one test; test.urine_pcr and test.abi are added but no profile, rule or care item uses them (CARE-DM-KIDNEY's fallback is the reagent strip, not the protein ratio). CARE-DM-KETONES and the kidney fallback depend on test.urinalysis_dipstick returning urine ketones and protein as components; the pack does not confirm that it does.
why: A test whose result concept is missing or partial produces results that no atom can read, so the differential and evidence stay empty after the result returns. Capability ids are what make a site-unavailable test show as unavailable rather than as a gap.
fix: Rewrite each entry in the test catalogue shape with components[], fasting_required and capability_id (cap.ogtt, a ketone meter, blood gas, retinal camera). Give test.venous_gas both obs.ph_venous and obs.bicarbonate. Confirm test.urinalysis_dipstick lists obs.ketones_urine, obs.glucose_urine and obs.urine_protein_dipstick. Either use test.urine_pcr in the kidney fallback or drop it. Give the abdominal X-ray a report concept or mark it as report-only.

where: wiring/formulary.additions.json, drugs[] and classes[]
finding: No dose, strength or brand appears, which is right. But the 13 drug entries carry only id, generic, class and source: none has routes, methods, presentationsDraft, allergyGroups, the flags object, charts or the 'to-verify' dose skeleton that the live entry shape requires, and they use 'emhslu2023' text where the catalogue has the boolean onEmhsluDraft. Without flags, the kidney check (which runs only on drugs flagged renal) will not run for dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, sitagliptin, vildagliptin or glimepiride, and insulin aspart is not marked highAlert. The briefing describes the glucose chart rule as 'a sulfonylurea (glibenclamide, gliclazide)'; if that rule lists drugs, glimepiride would not open the chart. The fate of class oral_glucose_lowering after the split is not stated (dx.dm_type2 'keep' omits it and nothing removes it). Bendroflumethiazide has no source.
why: The generator test fails on drift and the Python validator on shape. A new sulfonylurea with no chart rule and no renal flag is a hypoglycaemia risk the system was built to catch.
fix: Supply complete entries in the live shape with every dose 'to-verify'. Set renal true for the gliflozins, gliptins, metformin and sulfonylureas, highAlert for every insulin, and charts ['mar','glucose'] for insulins and sulfonylureas. Change the glucose chart rule to class = sulfonylurea. State that oral_glucose_lowering is retired and migrate every reference to it.

where: wiring/formulary.additions.json, diagnosisLinks dx.dm_type2 (add: antiplatelet) and dx.diabetic_neuropathy
finding: 'antiplatelet' is linked to type 2 diabetes with no condition. The Plan shows linked classes on the problem card as treatment classes for that diagnosis. The neuropathy link names three classes that may not exist and adds no drugs for them.
why: An antiplatelet is for established cardiovascular disease, not for diabetes as such; showing it on every type 2 card invites primary-prevention aspirin and its bleeding risk. The pack's rule is drug names and classes only where the source names them for that indication.
fix: Remove antiplatelet from dx.dm_type2 and leave it on the cardiovascular diagnoses that already carry it. For neuropathy, add the classes and at least the EMHSLU-listed generic for each, or leave the link out until they exist.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-KETONES (when: vs.glucose >= REF-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST; problems include dx.dka)
finding: The only ketone item is hidden unless the capillary glucose is 18 mmol/L or more, including on the dx.dka problem card. It opens only the urine strip although test.ketones_blood is added to the menu, and it stays after a ketone result is recorded.
why: Ketoacidosis with a glucose below 18 (and below 11.1 on an SGLT2 inhibitor, in pregnancy or starvation) is the case the dx.dka note warns about: 'a normal or near-normal glucose does NOT argue against ketoacidosis'. On the ketoacidosis card the test that makes the diagnosis must always be offered.
fix: Split it: on dx.dka and dx.dm_type1 show 'Ketones now (blood where available, urine strip otherwise)' with no glucose condition, hidden once vs.ketones is recorded; on the other diabetes problems keep the 18 mmol/L condition and add 'or on an SGLT2 inhibitor and unwell'. Open test.ketones_blood with the strip as the stated fallback.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DKA-REFER (opens.disposition 'refer'; label 'hospital now')
finding: For dx.dka and dx.hhs the only care item is 'hospital now' and ticking it sets the disposition to 'refer'. MedSync is a hospital system and the differential rules run in the emergency and inpatient settings. In a hospital that treats these emergencies the item points the patient away, and EC-4 does not say whether ticking overwrites a disposition of 'admit' already chosen. Nothing sets senior review to 'now'.
why: The WHO HEARTS-D instruction is written for primary care. For a time-critical diagnosis the default action must be right for the site: escalate and admit here, or transfer if this site cannot manage it.
fix: Make the item site-aware through a capability condition: where the site can manage it, 'Senior review now; admit to a monitored bed' opening seniorReview 'now' and disposition 'admit'; otherwise 'Refer to hospital now' opening disposition 'refer'. Specify in EC-4 that 'opens' proposes a value and never overwrites one the clinician set.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-CONFIRM, CARE-HYPERGLYCAEMIA-FOLLOW-UP, CARE-GDM-POSTPARTUM, CARE-DKD-CONFIRM (opens.tests); profile dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia
finding: These items are for a test on a later day ('on another day', 'after recovery', 'after the birth at 6 to 12 weeks', 'at 3 months') but 'opens.tests' puts the order in today's basket, and the note cannot be signed until the basket is placed or emptied. For steroid-induced hyperglycaemia the item says 'fasting glucose after recovery' while the profile note says 'a fasting value can be normal: test after lunch or before the evening meal' and the dossier (REF-DM-SUS-STEROID) says postprandial or random, not fasting. For dx.ckd and dx.diabetic_kidney_disease the only repeat offered is creatinine at 3 months.
why: A fasting glucose drawn today in an acutely ill or pregnant patient gives the stress or pregnancy value the item was meant to avoid. A fasting test on steroids can falsely reassure. A first-ever low eGFR with no earlier value may be acute kidney injury; the sources to check are NICE NG203 (early repeat of a first low eGFR) and KDIGO 2024 (do not assume chronicity from one value).
fix: Give the item shape a 'due' field so a deferred test is written as follow-up or a dated future order, not today's order. For steroid-induced hyperglycaemia change the test to an afternoon or post-meal glucose. Add to the kidney problems 'First low eGFR with no earlier result: repeat soon to exclude acute kidney injury' with the interval taken from a signed reference the CSO chooses.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-EDU-HYPO, CARE-DM-EDU-SICK-DAY, CARE-DM-EDU-INSULIN (when: medicine_group insulin or sulfonylurea); problem dx.hypoglycaemia_dm
finding: The three teaching items appear only when insulin or a sulfonylurea is already in the medicines history. They do not appear at the visit where insulin or a sulfonylurea is first prescribed (the 'when' reads the history, not the Plan basket), and not for dx.dm_type1 when no medicine has been recorded yet. Sick-day teaching is limited to insulin although the pack's own reference REF-DM-RX-SGLT2-HOLD stops SGLT2 inhibitors during critical illness and prolonged fasting. The dx.hypoglycaemia_dm card carries only the chronic item 'Lows: ask at every visit ...' and nothing about recurrence after a low on a sulfonylurea or long-acting insulin, or about not sending the patient home after the first recovery.
why: The visit at which a hypoglycaemia-causing medicine starts is when the teaching matters most. Sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia recurs; UCG 2023 and the JBDS hypoglycaemia guideline are the sources to check for the observation step.
fix: Let these 'when' conditions also read prescriptions in the Plan basket; show the hypoglycaemia and sick-day items on dx.dm_type1 without a medicine condition; add an SGLT2 inhibitor sick-day item; add an acute item on dx.hypoglycaemia_dm for the cause, the medicine responsible and observation before discharge, routed and worded from the source, with no treatment instruction.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json, the list as a whole (18 items on a dx.dm_type2 card); CARE-DM-BP, CARE-DM-HYPO-REVIEW, CARE-DM-TARGET, CARE-DM-FOOT, CARE-DM-EYE, CARE-DM-TYPE1-REFER, CARE-DKD-RASI
finding: No item knows whether its check is due. Yearly and two-yearly checks (kidney, lipids, eye, foot risk) and HbA1c show at every visit whatever was done last month, because the list uses no result-age condition and EC-1 makes an out-of-window result 'unknown', so 'not done within the interval' cannot be written. Several items are two actions under one tick, one of them a prescribing decision: CARE-DM-BP 'Blood pressure today; treat towards below 130/80' and CARE-DM-HYPO-REVIEW 'ask at every visit; ... relax the target for now'. CARE-DM-TARGET says 'record it' but there is nowhere to record a target. Labels claim conditions that no predicate tests: CARE-DM-TYPE1-REFER 'in a new diagnosis' (shown for every type 1, including long-standing), CARE-DKD-RASI 'albuminuria with raised blood pressure'. CARE-DM-FOOT says 'full risk assessment every year' although the existing iwgdf_risk classifier gives 1 to 3 months for the highest category. CARE-DM-EYE gives the type 2 schedule to type 1 as well.
why: Pack rules 9 and 10: do not cry wolf; a label says exactly what its predicates test. Eighteen boxes that never change teach clinicians to tick all or none, and a tick on a compound item records nothing definite. A blood-pressure target inside a tick-box is a treatment decision presented as a task.
fix: Add a 'recorded_within {concept or item, ref}' atom so screening items show only when due or never recorded, and show the date of the last one. Split compound items: 'Blood pressure measured today' (tick) and a separate review item with requiresPrescribing true whose target comes from a signed reference. Add 'when' conditions that match each label, or shorten the label. Take the foot interval from iwgdf_risk. Give CARE-DM-TARGET a field to write to or drop 'record it'.

where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json 'where_unavailable' on CARE-DM-HBA1C, CARE-DM-KIDNEY, CARE-DM-EYE; profiles dx.diabetic_kidney_disease, dx.ckd, dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia; wiring/formulary.additions.json check.metformin_no_egfr
finding: The three district alternatives are sensible as far as they go, but: the kidney fallback ('Urine reagent strip; a positive is sent for a laboratory ratio') does not say that a negative strip does not exclude early kidney disease and gives no fallback for creatinine; CARE-DM-HBA1C's fallback prints a catalogue id in display text ('Order test.glucose_fasting ...'); CARE-DM-CVD-RISK names the laboratory chart with no fallback where cholesterol is unavailable; CARE-DM-KETONES, CARE-DPN-EXCLUDE and CARE-DKD-CONFIRM have none. The kidney profiles accept only UACR and eGFR as evidence, although obs.urine_protein_dipstick exists, so a district site can never show evidence for kidney disease. dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia accepts only laboratory results, so a meter-only site cannot reach it. The proposed check 'metformin and no eGFR in the last 12 months' would fire on every metformin prescription for ever at a site with no creatinine.
why: Pack rule 8 and briefing Part 4.1: every test-dependent step names its capability and gives a district pathway that reaches a safe answer; not assessed is not normal. A negative strip recorded as 'kidney check done' is a false negative for the range the screen exists to find.
fix: Make 'where_unavailable' a structured field keyed by capability, shown only at sites without it. Word the kidney fallback 'Urine reagent strip now; a negative strip does not exclude early kidney disease; refer for a laboratory ratio and creatinine yearly'. Add a reagent-strip protein atom to both kidney profiles and a capillary fasting atom to dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia. Give the cardiovascular risk item its non-laboratory fallback with the dossier's caveat. Make check.metformin_no_egfr capability-aware.

where: clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json past_history.condition_details.diabetes, property 'type' option 'pregnancy_only'; wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json hx.prior_gdm (restrictedClass sexual_reproductive_health) and hx.dm_type_reported
finding: The pack's own addendum classes previous gestational diabetes as a restricted (sexual and reproductive health) fact, but the history amendment captures the same fact as an ordinary option under 'About the diabetes', composes it into the note sentence ('Diabetes (Only in pregnancy) ...') and carries it as a qualifier on the problem-list proposal; hx.dm_type_reported lists 'gestational' unrestricted. Separately, a woman whose only diabetes was in pregnancy has past condition diabetes = yes, so every rule that reads that answer treats her as a known diabetic: the urgent hypoglycaemia flag for level 1 values, SUG-PMH-DIABETES, 'pmh:diabetes' evidence on dx.dm_type2, dx.dka, dx.hhs and the complication profiles, and a problem-list proposal of diabetes.
why: Pack rule 7: a restricted class must not leak into patient-facing text and must travel with any rule that reads it. If the classification in the addendum stands this is a breach; if it does not, the addendum is wrong. Either way the two files disagree. Previous gestational diabetes is a risk factor, not established diabetes.
fix: Decide the classification once with the CSO. Move 'diabetes only in pregnancy' out of the diabetes detail block into its own past-history question (restricted if that is the decision, with the lock and clinical-only composition), and make it a risk-factor atom for the suspect rules rather than 'past_condition diabetes yes'.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json items.amend ex.eyes_ent_neck.fundoscopy (attributes method, view, dr_grade, macula); named_scales.add.icdr_dr in 09-diagnosis.amendment.json
finding: The new 'view' attribute duplicates the existing option seen = not_visualised, so the two can contradict each other. The rule text says 'a grade is offered only when the view is adequate', but shown_when tests only seen includes diabetic_retinopathy. There is no way to record 'no retinopathy' as a grade after an adequate dilated examination or photograph: dr_grade has no 'none' option, while the NCD feature retinopathy_stage and REF-EX-DR-RECALL both have one. The diagnosis scale icdr_dr offers 'no apparent retinopathy' as a severity of diabetic retinopathy. Numbers in the grade hint (20 haemorrhages, 4, 2 and 1 quadrants) are thresholds outside any reference entry, and the labels 'Severe (4-2-1)' and 'IRMA' are not plain wording.
why: If a normal adequate screen cannot be recorded, exam.retinopathy_grade is never written as 'none', the eye screen can never be shown as done and normal, and the screening prompt never clears. A grade recorded on an inadequate view is false precision.
fix: Fold 'view' and the existing not_visualised into one attribute. Show dr_grade when view = adequate AND method is dilated or photograph, with options none, mild, moderate, severe, proliferative; keep 'no retinopathy seen (undilated)' as a composed finding that writes no grade. Remove 'no apparent retinopathy' from the diagnosis severity scale. Move the grade definition to a signed reference shown as the hint and write the labels in full words.

where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST, FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT, FLAG-EX-KETONES-RISK; clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json FLAG-DM-ADMITTED-RECENT
finding: FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST uses the badge text 'Glucose {glucose}', the same as the existing glucose flags; same-text badges merge, so its reason ('test urine ketones now') may be lost under FLAG-EX-GLU-HIGH. It has no glucose context and no capability condition, so it stays up for ever at a site with no ketone strips. FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT says 'within the ICO window', which is not plain wording and gives no interval. FLAG-DM-ADMITTED-RECENT says 'review sick-day rules and insulin supply' for an admission that may have been a hyperosmolar state in someone on tablets.
why: A flag whose message is merged away or cannot be acted on is noise. Levels are otherwise reasonable: caution for the ketone prompt, the at-risk ketone band, retinopathy referral and both history flags is right.
fix: Give the ketone prompt its own badge ('Glucose {glucose}: test ketones') and hide it where the site has no ketone test, showing 'refer' instead. Write the interval from the classifier result into the retinopathy reason. Reword the admission flag to 'review sick-day rules and the supply of medicines'.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json rules DDX-RESULT-EGFR, DDX-RESULT-UACR, DDX-GLUCOSE-IN-HOSPITAL, DDX-RETINOPATHY, ddx_rules.amend DDX-GLUCOSE-HIGH; profile dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed
finding: DDX-RESULT-EGFR puts dx.aki first as must-not-miss on an eGFR up to 365 days old. DDX-RESULT-UACR and DDX-RESULT-EGFR suggest dx.diabetic_kidney_disease in people with no diabetes recorded. DDX-GLUCOSE-IN-HOSPITAL fires in known diabetics and suggests 'hyperglycaemia, unconfirmed' for them. dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed uses the in-hospital threshold (7.8) with no setting condition, so an outpatient random value of 7.9 is suggested evidence. Adding two more chips to DDX-GLUCOSE-HIGH may push others past the eight shown.
why: These are chips, not flags, so the cost is clutter and a label that says more than its predicate; but an old result should not raise an acute must-not-miss.
fix: Give the acute kidney injury suggestion a short result age from a signed reference; add past diabetes yes or a diabetes diagnosis on the board to the diabetic kidney disease suggestion; add 'past diabetes not recorded yes' handling to the in-hospital rule; add the setting condition to the profile atom.

where: clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json condition_details.diabetes properties and composer; clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json items.add
finding: treatment: 'diet_only' is exclusive, so 'diet only' and 'herbal or traditional' cannot both be recorded. lows_12_months options are in the first person ('Yes, treated it myself') in a form the clinician fills. There is no 'not sure' for lows or admissions. The composer template leaves empty brackets and stray punctuation when properties are unanswered. ex.skin.injection_sites composes 'lipohypertrophy at injection sites' for a finding labelled 'Lumps or thickening', an interpretation rather than the finding, and is not placed in a part of the skin system. ex.eyes_ent_neck.visual_acuity has ids containing '/', no phrase for one eye recorded, an unclear 'pinhole' flag, and no place for 'not tested: no chart'. The urine ketone options stop at 3+ where some strips read 4+.
why: Ground rules: findings not interpretations; plain en-GB wording; an unanswered property is an absent key and must not leave marks in the note.
fix: Make only 'none' exclusive; write options in the third person; build the sentence clause by clause as the property phrases already allow; compose 'lumps or thickening at injection sites'; record acuity per eye with 'unaided, with glasses, with pinhole' and safe ids.

where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json profile notes (dx.dm_type2, dx.dm_type1, dx.diabetic_kidney_disease, dx.gestational_diabetes, dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia)
finding: Notes state local epidemiology and forward-looking claims with no source key in the profile's sources: 'a third of Ugandan adults with non-autoimmune diabetes are lean', 'most young Ugandans with clinical type 1 are antibody negative', 'creatinine-based eGFR overestimated kidney function in Ugandan adults', 'WHO is revising these criteria in late 2026'. dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia lists test.hba1c to decide while its note says HbA1c waits 3 months after steroids stop. Notes carry many thresholds as prose (11.1, 6/12, 3 months, 2 of 3 samples, 6 to 12 weeks, eGFR below 30).
why: Briefing Part 4.1: nothing clinical without a citation; no invented prevalence figures. The claims may well be right, but a CSO cannot sign what has no source.
fix: Add the source key for each claim to the profile's sources and to sourcesToAdd, or remove the sentence. Remove test.hba1c from the steroid profile or mark it 'after 3 months'. Reference thresholds in notes by their entry.
